notes.text: They dressed 11 forwards and 7 defensemen in 4 of their last 10 games, including the last one. Nikita Kucherov takes shifts on two lines, L1 and L2. Victor Hedman is the seventh defenseman, rotating in mostly beside Lilleberg and Crozier.

The forward lines keep changing. Even their four most-used trios over the last 10 games cover only 31% of their forwards’ 5-on-5 time, the 8th-lowest in the league (a typical team: 38%). The lines listed lean on their latest games, but expect new combinations tonight.
Pontus Holmberg is out four weeks (lower body injury) and missed their last game. He is one of their more valuable skaters. Yanni Gourde has taken his spot beside Zemgus Girgensons and Ilya Mikheyev.
Erik Černák is out (illness) and has missed the last 2 games. Emil Lilleberg has taken his spot beside Ryan McDonagh.

stakes: The Lightning go in tied for third in the Atlantic with 32 points, a point behind the Panthers, second. A regulation win for the Lightning would lift them past the Panthers.

story.head: Something has to give
paras: The Panthers have won three straight, while the Lightning are on a three-game losing streak. This is an Atlantic Division matchup, with the Lightning third (tied for ninth in the NHL) and the Panthers second (tied for seventh).

This season, the Panthers have outscored teams 84-76, even though they’ve been outscored 50-44 at 5-on-5. On special teams, they’ve outscored teams 26-18, and only one team creates more chances on the power play.

Both teams rarely ice the puck and don’t block many shots. The Lightning keep shots away better than almost anyone (3rd). As for the Panthers, they forecheck harder than anyone (1st). Something has to give when the Lightning’s shooting runs into the Panthers’ defense. Beyond that, the Bolts wait for good looks, but the Panthers settle for hopeful ones.

Nikita Kucherov (10 G / 23 A / 33 P in 25 GP) leads the Lightning in scoring. Jake Guentzel (15 G / 16 A / 31 P in 25 GP) has a team-high 15 goals, tied for seventh in the NHL, with seven points in his last five games. Matthew Tkachuk (7 G / 28 A / 35 P in 26 GP) leads the Panthers in scoring and is sixth in the NHL. Sam Reinhart (12 G / 11 A / 23 P in 26 GP) has a team-high twelve goals, with eight goals in ten games against Tampa Bay since 2023-24.
Andrei Vasilevskiy (11-6-1 / .897 SV% in 18 GS) is expected to start for Tampa Bay, and Akira Schmid (6-3-2 / .885 SV% in 10 GS) for Florida.
